## Download and use this snapshot

This page describes the published files in `nicktempleman/csoai-gspc-drift`. Treat them as a dated snapshot: use the observation dates and limitations in the files and source notes below. A page edit does not refresh the measurements.

With the Kaggle CLI installed and authenticated:

```bash
kaggle datasets download -d nicktempleman/csoai-gspc-drift -p ./dataset --unzip
```

Start by inspecting `drift_rail.json`. Keep its original bytes and record the Kaggle version before transforming or comparing results.

Published files include:

- `README.md`
- `eval.yaml`
- `manifest.jsonl`
- `drift_rail.json`

[Current GSPC board](https://councilof.ai/api/gspc) · [Methodology](https://councilof.ai/methodology/) · [Verify supported signed records](https://councilof.ai/gspc-verify/) · [Corrections](https://councilof.ai/claim-maintenance)

# GSPC drift rail — day-over-day consistency

A longitudinal consistency signal over signed boards. `drift_rail.json` states its own
method in the file: day-over-day best-score delta on MEASURED boards with `n>=30`, thin-n boards excluded,
**no model judges** anywhere in the computation — the predicates are deterministic. Per axis it records the
boards in the window, the window bounds, and the deltas between consecutive timestamps. Drift is a
consistency signal, not a certification.

## Dataset facts (checked 2026-11-20)

- Kaggle version 4, last updated 2026-10-06.
- 4 files, 33,161 bytes. File types: .md (1), .json (1), .yaml (1), .jsonl (1).
- Hugging Face twin: [csoai/gspc-drift](https://huggingface.co/datasets/csoai/gspc-drift). 3 of 4 files have the same byte size there.
- Expected update frequency: never.
